headline: Members agreed to plant two serviceberry trees at 117 Leavitt Street and approved the September 14 minutes.

decision_titles: Replacement serviceberry trees at 117 Leavitt Street
plain_text:
1 
 
 
MINUTES OF THE SALEM TREE COMMISSION 
MONDAY, OCTOBER 19, 2026 
 
A meeting of the Salem Tree Commission was held on October 19, 2026, at 7:00 p.m., via ZOOM, 
an online video conference call system in accordance with Chapter 2 of the Acts of 2025. 
1. Present were Chair Darleen Melis; Members: Cady Goldfield, Paul L’Heureux, David 
Livingston, Rachel McCarter, Jacob St. Louis and Susan Yochelson; Tree Warden Kieran 
Kavanaugh and Commission Clerk Joanne Roomey. Absent were Vice Chair Kirt Rieder 
and Jessica Choi.  
2. Report – Kieran Kavanaugh, Tree Warden 
Kieran provided an update on September activities and ongoing projects. During September, 
the department received 19 emergency tree calls, the majority of which resulted from the 
September 26–28 nor'easter. Of those calls, eight involved tree failures, while the remaining 
calls involved limb or leader-related issues. 
Regarding fall planting, the department completed seven internal plantings and an additional 
26 plantings through a Community Development Block Grant. The department hopes to 
increase the number of internal plantings each year, particularly now that the Tree Department 
has three full-time staff members. 
The department is currently focused on pruning and removing unhealthy trees identified due 
to recent storm activity, with an emphasis on making city rights-of-way as safe as possible 
ahead of the winter season. Kieran also reported holding an introductory meeting with several 
Ward Councilors to discuss the possibility of a native planting ordinance. The discussion 
included shrubs, ground cover, and tree species. Reference was made to the Salem Tree 
Manual, including its recommended planting guidelines, list of unsuitable species, and 
invasive species list. The primary goal of the initial discussion was to encourage flexibility in 
species selection rather than requiring specific species. The department emphasized that the 
discussion was preliminary, with no formal proposal or decisions made. The meeting also 
involved several other city departments as part of a broader discussion of current practices 
and procedures. 
Darleen asked about tree removals near 12 Franklin Street. Google Maps images were 
reviewed to identify trees of some caliper right next to the road nearer to the old HMA site. 
Also photos were shared of a Protected Tree being removed Saturday evening over the holiday 
weekend. Kieran will investigate further. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
DOMINICK PANGALLO                 
MAYOR 
 
 
CITY OF SALEM, MASSACHUSETTS 
TREE COMMISSION 
57 ORNE STREET 
  SALEM, MA  01970 
TEL. 978-745-0195 FAX 978-741-7041 
 
Touch the Future – Plant a Tree 
 
 
 
 
DARLEEN MELIS, CHAIR 
KIRT RIEDER, VICE CHAIR 
 
KIERAN KAVANAUGH 
       TREE WARDEN
2 
A Memorandum of Agreement is being developed with the property owner of 59 Boston 
Street that will address the trees removed from the site and what trees will be planted as 
replacements. Once signed, Kieran will share the details. 
At 28 Norman Street (the former White Hen Pantry and now the E-Market) two large callery 
pear trees were removed and replaced with a row of bushes. As Protected Trees, despite insect 
damage, Kieran will pursue a conversation with the owner about planting trees in the broad 
border. Possibly, Dave Bresnahan can offer trees to deal with the heat island effect of the 
parking lot. 
3. Greening the Gateway Cities Program – David Bresnahan, DCR Forester  
Dave provided an update on the fall planting season, noting that the crew is currently in its 
sixth week, with four weeks remaining. The crew has been working diligently to complete 
plantings before winter. 
Since September 8, approximately 55 trees have been planted on setback or private property 
in Salem. Nearly three times that number have been planted in Lynn, which has a larger 
planting area and has generated increased interest from residents. 
Ten shade trees were planted at Loring Hills Condominium on Loring Circle in South Salem. 
Four of these trees may technically be considered public shade trees located along Loring 
Hills Avenue . However, watering and maintenance will be the responsibility of the  
condominium association and its maintenance staff. No other trees have been planted in the 
public right-of-way in Salem this fall. 
Dave reported ordering ten 2-inch balled-and-burlapped (B&B) trees for planting in Salem in 
November. Most will replace trees previously planted by the DCR that did not survive, 
including trees at Rainbow Terrace and Riley Plaza. 
Dave also ordered two serviceberry trees  ‘Robin Hill’ to plant at 117 Leavitt Street, on the 
Congress Street side, beneath utility wires. These trees replace two Kousa dogwoods 
previously planted by Conor Morgan in spring 2024 as part of a North Shore  Community 
Development Coalition tree permit (DPST-23-30).  
Darleen had previously indicated that North Shore CDC should be responsible for replacing 
the failed trees. Dave stated that the serviceberry trees have already been ordered and that he 
is willing to plant them; however, if the commission prefers to hold North Shore CDC 
responsible for the replacements, he can use the trees at another location.  Commission 
members agreed that the trees should be planted and that Kieran will have to talk to the CDC 
to resolve the tree failure that occurred within the required two year guideline. 
Dave is interested in developing a winter public tree project. He suggested that the tree lawn 
between Washington Street southbound and the Riley Plaza parking lot might be a good spot 
for replacing trees in steep decline.  Discussion suggested that the Washington Street median 
strip in front of the Indian restaurant might also need replacement trees.
3 
4. Centerboard Project / Holyoke Ins. Building – Bonnie Henry  
Bonnie Henry appeared before the commission and provided an overview of the new 
Centerboard family shelter project at the Holyoke Building. She presented a photograph of a 
Beech tree from 1993 and explained that the project presents a significant opportunity to 
replace a major shade tree on the property. 
Bonnie stated that her goal was to bring the existing site conditions and identified challenges 
to the commission’s attention, engage members in the project, and seek their advice and 
assistance. She noted that Centerboard is willing to consider and implement the commission’s 
recommendations. 
Bonnie also presented a site schematic from a recent walkthrough to orient the commission 
to the property, identifying Holyoke Square, Norman Street, Summer Street, and Gedney 
Street. She noted that there are approximately 16 city-owned trees surrounding the property, 
but that the site presents several significant challenges. 
Kieran stated that he was present to assist with the removal of the Norway Maple and agreed 
with the site plan presented. He will assess the trees on the property and identify any unhealthy 
specimens, particularly those that may present safety concerns. He noted that fall planting 
plans are currently being finalized and that attention will then turn to spring planting 
opportunities. 
Steve Duffy, the contractor, and the project’s CEO  Mark DeJoie  and COO Heather 
Hildebrand are available to assist with the project and are willing to work with the 
commission. It was clarified that the private property begins at the location of the pear trees. 
Since the property is privately owned, permission is not required to plant trees; however, 
permission would be required for tree removal. 
Bonnie appeared before the commission seeking recommendations regarding appropriate tree 
species for planting and welcomed any guidance or suggestions the commission could 
provide. 
Darleen raised concerns regarding the elm tree located at the corner of Holyoke Square and 
Norman Street. She noted that during the Tree Steward event at that location the tree was 
found to have been planted eight inches too deep and will not survive under those conditions. 
Cady commented that the roots could be pruned to assist the removal but recommended 
waiting until the tree becomes dormant before attempting to dig it up.  Kieran will check 
beneath the mulch and assess if anything can be done. 
Darleen suggested that Bonnie coordinate directly with Kieran and Mark DeJoie  and Heather 
Hildebrand to discuss the tree concerns and planting recommendations. 
Centerboard Property Background  - The original purchaser had planned to develop the 
property into condominiums; however, the building’s layout turned out not to be suited to that 
purpose. Soon the property became unkempt. The Holyoke portion was leased to Centerboard 
as a shelter and now Centerboard owns the whole property.
4 
The property is currently under construction and is being renovated to provide family shelter 
services. The program serves families experiencing homelessness and is designed to help 
residents regain stability and get back on their feet within a six-month period. Approximately 
60% of the residents are under the age of 18. Maria Connell and the Salem Garden Club will 
be helping with smaller plantings in coordination with the shelter’s maintenance staff. 
Bonnie emphasized the need for suggestions and assistance from the commission regarding 
the property's landscaping and tree-planting opportunities to make this a beautiful part of the 
city. 
5. Tree Permit Visibility on City Website – Tree removals at 12 Franklin St. 
Darleen asked how the city can better inform property owners about the Tree Ordinance and 
make them aware of the requirements that apply to tree removals. 
Kieran suggested continuing outreach efforts to communicate the requirements of the 
ordinance through other city departments and making the information more visible on the 
city's website. The commission also discussed the possibility of distributing an informational 
flyer through the Water Department to help raise awareness among property owners. 
6. Trees and Sustainability – solar panels 
Darleen reported that the Planning Department and the City Council are  reviewing the 
possibility of rooftop wind turbines . A comment from the Historical Commission indicates 
that since their board has not been approached on this topic, they would prefer that any 
legislation delay until consultations can occur  regarding their visual impact on historic 
properties. 
Darleen noted that the installation of wind turbines should not come at the expense of existing 
trees similar to the concerns raised by the installation of solar panels. In both cases, the vital 
15 points of benefits listed in the Tree Ordinance outweigh the single purposes of such 
technological infrastructure. The commission did not discuss the sustainability codes in detail. 
Further discussion is expected at the November meeting when Kirt attends. 
7. Tree Replacement – 329 Essex St. elm replaced hophornbeam under overhead wires 
Darleen shared her screen showing an American Hophornbeam (Ostrya virginiana) planted in  
November 2025 at 329 Essex Street. She noted that the location has overhead utility wires 
and questioned the selection of an elm as the replacement tree, as it may eventually interfere 
with the wires. 
The commission discussed the general policy of planting the largest appropriate tree possible 
while taking existing overhead wires and site conditions into consideration. 
Kieran stated that the tree may have been replaced through one of the city's grant programs 
and agreed to investigate the specific planting to confirm.
5 
8. Future Tree Plantings on Salem Common 
Kieran reported that he has received an updated proposal for future tree plantings on Salem 
Common. Once the proposal has been approved and signed, he will be able to provide 
additional details regarding the implementation and execution of the project. The propo sal 
requires three signatures: the DPS Director, the Mayor, and the Superintendent of Parks. 
9.  Approve Tree Commission Minutes of September 14, 2026 
Ms. McCarter moved to approve the Tree Commission Meeting Minutes for September 14, 
2026. Seconded by Mr. St. Louis . A roll call vote was taken, and the motion was carried. 
David Livingston and Cady Goldfield abstained. 
10. New Business - None 
Who has the Tree City USA flag?  Paul L’Heureux has the flag and will deliver to Darleen , 
who will get it back to Kieran. 
11. Questions from the audience - None 
12. Next Meeting Dates: Monday, November 16, 2026 at 7:00 p.m. and December 21, 2026 
via Zoom. 
13. Adjournment: There being no further business to come before the Tree Commission this 
evening, Mr. St. Louis moved to adjourn. Seconded by Mr. L’Heureux. A roll call vote was 
taken, and the motion was carried unanimously. The meeting was adjourned at 8:15 p.m. 
Respectfully submitted, 
 
 
Joanne M. Roomey 
Commission Clerk 
 
 
 
 
Know your rights under the Open Meeting Law M.G.L. c. 30A §18-25 and City Ordinance 
Sections 2-2028 through 2-2033
